description: Golden media for the LTX/H3 benchmark. The media itself is NOT in git; this manifest is the committed artifact and the files live beside it under benchmarks/assets/. Verify with: uv run python apps/worker/scripts/golden_pack.py --verify
rules: Every acquired asset carries a SHA256. A mismatch STOPS the comparison — LTX from image A and H3 from image A-as-re-exported are not a comparison.
Provenance and licence are required before an asset may be marked acquired. Prefer internally created or generated media we hold rights to; never a commercial track pulled from the internet.
One identity across every reference-person framing. The comparison is identity retention, so the identity must be the constant.
Do not re-encode an acquired asset. Re-encoding changes the hash and silently changes the input.

assets.purpose: The single frozen song for every music-video cell and every lip-sync measurement.
assets.provenance: Generated 2026-08-24 by our own ACE-Step service (acestep-v15-xl-turbo, LM acestep-5Hz-lm-4B, repo commit 6d467e4) on Vast instance C.48538452, from lyrics written by us for lip-sync measurement. No commercial track and no third-party rights. Take 2 of 2; take 1 had no usable instrumental gap. Full generation settings and the lyric sheet are in benchmark-song.lyrics.json.
assets.notes: FORMAT DEVIATION: manifest originally specified .wav. ACE-Step's API encodes to MP3 before returning and exposes no format switch, so MP3 is what production produces and what both LTX A2V and H3 fully_copy actually receive; a WAV here would be less representative. 44100 Hz stereo, 192 kbps, 120.032653 s. VERIFIED: vocals present (gliding formants with vibrato at 400-950 Hz), structural break at ~53-55 s, content ends ~117 s with ~3 s trailing silence. NOT YET VERIFIED: exact vocal onset/offset and whether the break is vocal-free for >=2 s - a spectrogram cannot separate voice from guitar. Settle with a vocal separator or one listen before treating these as lip-sync ground truth.

assets.purpose: The exact lyrics, language, section structure and vocal onset/offset timings of benchmark-song.wav.
assets.provenance: Written by us on 2026-08-24 specifically for lip-sync measurement; frozen alongside the audio it describes.
assets.notes: Whisper must not be the source of truth here — it called an English pop song Khmer once. Vocal presence comes from a Demucs stem, and the sheet is what was actually sung.
